title: Johann Heinrich Kauderbach (The Hague) to Dresden, 1754-56, intercepted despatches with passages in figures (KHA Prins Willem V inv. 201, DECODE R1043-R2082)

steps.what: DECODE records fetched with the session cookie: 32 page images, 3 transcriptions (R1043, R1044, R2078).
Web search for a printed decipherment or edition of Kauderbach's despatches.
Digit counts, successor table, 2- and 3-figure phase IC on the DECODE transcriptions: no fixed period; long exact repeats show a fixed code.
Seven records transcribed from the images by sub-agents (one died on an oversized-image error and was re-run); R1954 in a letter-like hand only partly reliable.
Mixed 1/2/3-figure group rules by first digit scored by entropy; EM segmentation of 1-4-figure tokens.
Removing 5 and 8 as single-figure nulls restores a clean 2-figure phase (IC 0.027 vs 0.021; 4-figure 0.155/0.161 vs 0.103); Viterbi realignment gives a table of about 60 two-figure codes.

Homophonic letter solver (quadgram coordinate ascent, validated 98% on synthetic French through the same pipeline) in French, German, Dutch, Italian, word-reversed French, with nulls, syllable values or merged look-alike figures.
Pattern cribs for long repeats (guerre, Angleterre) seeded into the solver.

DECODE key listing searched; Kauderbach's 1761 key (R936) fetched: one code per letter or syllable, capitals for names, a declared null. Numbers do not fit; vocabulary adopted (m restored from the image).
Simulated annealing over one-to-one assignments of the codes onto the 1761 vocabulary, char-4-gram score; seeds 22 and 24 converged to the same key (-3.85/letter).
Key refined by reading and an extended vocabulary (in, ou, qu, st, par, pas, qui, pour, fai, ke, z; 01/12 swapped); ten letters read by two sub-agents, one per five letters.
Content checked against history: Holderness's warning and the 30,000-man augmentation (Jul 1755), Kniphausen at Compiegne, the Treaty of Versailles of 1 May 1756 with its neutrality clause.

Four slips of normalisation in the reading files and write-up, reported while quotations were pulled for Lasry's list, re-checked group by group in cipher/R*.txt with key.json and the machine decryptions, and corrected: R1043 'parce qu'on craint qu'il n'y ait des articles secrets qui aillent encore plus loin' (was 'croit qu'il y a ... qui vont') and 'l'on a fait aussi' (was 'dit'); R2080 'treize mille hommes' (29 03 14 77 16, confirmed on the image; was 'trente', so the augmentation of the verification step above is 13,000, not 30,000) and 'pour combatre' (66 = pour; was 'et combattre').

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 8509 tokens, 60 types, fr-modern order 4: reading -2.364 per letter; random keys -5.279 (z 10.0); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.522 (mean -3.531, z 107.9); annealer on the real text -2.403. Verdict: pass.
Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): cipher/R*.txt with the hand readings read/R*.txt and the machine readings read/machine_R*.txt; key key.json.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.286; polyphony 0.0; 3 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.403

outcome.method_basis: Nulls and the two-figure code table were found by statistics, and the code values were recovered by simulated annealing onto the plaintext vocabulary (letters and syllables) of Kauderbach's 1761 key (DECODE R936), whose numbers do not fit this 1754-58 table.
outcome.notes: fraction_read = share of the 8,512 groups carrying a key value (only 10, 20, 40, 90 guessed, 12 occurrences). Readers estimate 65-97% of the text read in sense per letter; R1954 weakest; the clear sigla are read from context only.

credits.note: Kauderbach's 1761 key (HStAD, DECODE R936) used for its plaintext vocabulary; numbers do not fit

texts.label: R2078, 23 Dec 1754
texts.summary: Kauderbach, Saxon-Polish resident at The Hague, to Dresden: the States of Holland face their most difficult deliberations in years, the Comte d'Affry's overture on one side and Colonel Yorke's memorial asking what the Republic's engagements amount to on the other.

texts.label: R1958, 20 June 1755
texts.summary: Colonel Yorke assures Kauderbach that his court is well disposed to renewing the subsidy treaty, and that he will second Saxon interests at The Hague with all his strength; if the transport of [Q.] arrives safely there will be no war in Europe. (Bracketed sigla are clear abbreviations whose 1754 meanings are not all settled.)

texts.label: R2079, 6 July 1755
texts.summary: Haslang tells the Bavarian resident he has Newcastle's word that his subsidy treaty will be renewed; the prospects for the augmentation fade, which Kauderbach thinks will help the renewal of subsidies. (Bracketed sigla are clear abbreviations whose 1754 meanings are not all settled.)

texts.label: R2080, 22 July 1755
texts.summary: The arguments raised in the States of Holland against the proposed augmentation of thirteen thousand men urged by Lord Holderness: it would not suffice against the danger, the danger must first be established, and the other provinces must contribute equally.

texts.label: R1959, 5 Aug 1755
texts.summary: The rumour that [E.M.] is negotiating with [P.] seems not wholly unfounded and is spread by the [M.] party in Amsterdam; the ambassador of [Q.] sounds Kauderbach about a subsidy treaty, and he refers him to the Saxon minister in Paris. (Bracketed sigla are clear abbreviations whose 1754 meanings are not all settled.)

texts.label: R2081, 12 Aug 1755
texts.summary: The [P.] are as dissatisfied with [J. C.] as with [S.] and suspect [U.] of not truly embracing their measures, though [U.] is constrained by her situation at home and abroad; a sudden move had been expected from [Q.]. (Bracketed sigla are clear abbreviations whose 1754 meanings are not all settled.)

texts.label: R2082, 15 Aug 1755
texts.summary: The ambassador of [Q.] says [E.M.] wrote to his king in his own hand of an army of 150,000 men; [P.] declares it will abandon the continent if no defensive measures are taken here; [U.] will push the augmentation at the next assembly. (Bracketed sigla are clear abbreviations whose 1754 meanings are not all settled.)

texts.label: R1044, 29 Sept 1755
texts.summary: Members of the States complain that [P.] takes so many prizes in Europe without giving a reason, fearing [G.] will use it as a pretext to fall on the Low Countries; the [M.] party credits its prince with [G.]'s moderation there. (Bracketed sigla are clear abbreviations whose 1754 meanings are not all settled.)

texts.label: R1954, March 1756 (with N.21 of 16 March 1756)
texts.summary: Fragmentary reading (weak transcription): Holland has not yet deliberated on Colonel Yorke's requisition or on d'Affry's memorial, and the deliberation will stay suspended until [Q.] has explained itself on the representations [W.] made to the Comte d'Affry. (Bracketed sigla are clear abbreviations whose 1754 meanings are not all settled.)

texts.label: R1043, 25 May 1756
texts.summary: Certain news that the long-rumoured treaty was signed at Versailles on the 2nd of the month: neutrality of the Low Countries, no help to the other party's enemy, and reportedly an undertaking about the election of a King of the Romans; it caused consternation at The Hague for fear of secret articles.

prior.where: DECODE notes that the Hague cabinet never solved them; no printed decipherment found.

human: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login and passed its session cookie to the model, set up Claude Code with Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.
